content:
We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume). Need JSON route.

We have target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need break into precursors.

From apply_template 1664101 gave two precursors: a large complex molecule (CN(...)) and Cc1ccc(N)cc1 (p-toluidine). The large one is not commercially available likely expensive. Not good.

Template 1205701 gave a precursor where amide N is substituted with N(C(=O)CCc3ccccc3) etc. Also not simple.

We need maybe disconnection at sulfonamide bond: break between sulfonyl and aniline. That yields sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. The sulfonyl part attached to aromatic ring with vinyl amide side chain.

So we could propose: Step1: Couple sulfonyl chloride with aniline (p-toluidine). So precursors: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc1 . But is sulfonyl chloride commercially available? We checked is_buyable false. Might not be.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation via sulfonic acid + SOCl2 in situ, but we need commercially available sulfonic acid? Maybe 4-(2-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acryloyl)anilino)benzenesulfonic acid? Not likely.

Maybe break at amide: produce aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acid chloride of cinnamic acid derivative? The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So break amide gives aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N)?? Actually amide broken yields carboxylic acid derivative: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring. That is 4-(E)-cinnamoyl benzoic acid? Wait structure: aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) attached to sulfonyl and to vinyl amide side chain. The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. Breaking amide gives the aniline (c3ccccc3N) and the acid: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? Actually the amide is attached to the vinyl carbonyl: C(=O)N-aryl. So the carbonyl is attached to the vinyl chain which is attached to aromatic ring. So the acid would be: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. That is 4-(E)-cinnamic acid attached to sulfonyl phenyl. That might be commercially available? Possibly 4-(E)-cinnamic acid (cinnamic acid) is common, but with sulfonyl phenyl attached? Not.

Maybe break at the C=C double bond (retro-aldol) to give two fragments: aromatic aldehyde and something else. Might be complex.

Simplify: propose three-step route:

Step1: Synthesize sulfonyl chloride intermediate from commercially available 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually we need sulfonyl attached to phenyl with vinyl amide side chain. Could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) then do Suzuki coupling to attach the vinyl amide phenyl? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). That phenyl has the vinyl amide substituent at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . So sulfonyl attached to aniline (p-toluidine) via N-SO2-aryl. The sulfonyl phenyl also has the vinyl amide substituent para to the sulfonyl? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl via S(=O)2 attached to N of p-toluidine, and the phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl S as S(=O)2-aryl. That phenyl also has the vinyl amide substituent at para position.

Thus we could start from 4-bromo-phenylsulfonyl chloride (commercial) then do Suzuki coupling with vinyl amide phenyl boronic acid? Wait the substituent is /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to phenyl. That's a styryl amide. Could be made via Heck coupling of 4-bromo-phenylsulfonyl chloride with acrylamide? Actually the side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. Could be formed by Heck coupling of 4-bromo-phenylsulfonyl chloride with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Acrylamide is commercially available? Yes, acryloyl amide with phenyl? Actually we need acryloyl aniline (C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N). That's N-(2-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Wait the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with NH2 (aniline). So the amide is N-phenyl-2-propenamide (cinnamamide) with an extra NH2 on phenyl? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with NH2 at para? No it's an aniline (aniline) attached to carbonyl: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . That is an amide where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl that also has an NH2 substituent? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an extra N? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is a phenyl with two amino groups: one at position 1 (attached to carbonyl) and another at position? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (as substituent) and also there is an N attached to the aromatic carbon at the other end? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" means N attached to aromatic carbon (position 1) and also the aromatic carbon has an N attached (position maybe 4). So it's a diamino benzene (p-phenylenediamine) but one N is part of amide. So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH2 group (para). So the side chain is trans-cinnamoyl attached to p-phenylenediamine.

Thus building this may be complex.

Given limited time, maybe propose route using the template 1664101 which gave two precursors: a large complex molecule (maybe commercially available?) Let's check if that large molecule is buyable. Use is_buyable.
